title: Vishnu is born as Rama
hook: Dasharatha's long wait; God comes down as his son
carry: avatar: god comes down to set things right

segments.voice: Yesterday: sankat mochan, and a mountain carried through the night. You've met Hanuman. Now, for five weeks, the whole story he lives inside.

Ayodhya. A shining city on a river, with walls and gardens and elephants, and a good king named Dasharatha. His name means ten chariots. He has wealth, peace, and three queens: Kausalya, Kaikeyi and Sumitra. And no son. Year after year, the kingdom waits for an heir, and the king grows old. And far above Ayodhya, the gods have a problem of their own.

This is the opening of the Ramayana, the story of Rama. Tradition says Valmiki composed it, and calls him the first poet. For the next five weeks, i'll walk you through it, one scene a day. Here's the trouble above the clouds. A demon king, Ravana, has won a boon: no god, no demon, no spirit can kill him. He never thought to ask about humans; they seemed too small to matter. So the gods go to Vishnu, the preserver, and Vishnu makes a choice: he will be born as a human, as Dasharatha's son. Back on earth, Dasharatha holds a great fire ritual for sons, led by a young sage, Rishyashringa. Out of the flames rises a shining figure carrying a golden bowl of sweet rice pudding, payasa. Give this to your queens, he says. In time, four sons are born. Kausalya bears Rama. Kaikeyi bears Bharata. Sumitra bears twins, Lakshmana and Shatrughna. Remember the name Kaikeyi. Now, the big idea. Hindus call it avatara, a word that means coming down. Many Hindus believe that when the world tips badly out of balance, God doesn't only fix it from far away. God comes down, and is born as one of us: a baby, in a family, in a house with worried parents. Rama is honored as Vishnu's avatar. That's why, on Rama's birthday, Rama Navami, many temples and homes place a small image of baby Rama in a cradle and rock it at midday, the hour tradition gives for his birth. The old king asked for an heir. God came to live in his house.
screen: `RAVANA: NO GOD CAN KILL HIM.` · `VISHNU WILL BE BORN HUMAN.` · `A FIRE, A GOLDEN BOWL, FOUR SONS.` · `AVATARA: COMING DOWN.` · then, large: `AVATAR: GOD COMES DOWN TO SET THINGS RIGHT.`

segments.voice: Many Hindus repeat Rama's name as a prayer, softly, with the breath. Try it for a couple of minutes: breathe in, and as you breathe out, say Ram, out loud or in your head. If you'd rather not pray, picture your own ordinary rooms and ask what it would mean if the holy came to live right there, not far away.
Putrakameshti, the fire ritual for the wish of a son, after years of Dasharatha's waiting. A golden bowl comes from the flames, four sons are born, and the eldest, Rama, is Vishnu come down.
Your line: avatar, God comes down to set things right. Not only from far away: born into a family, in a house. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Many Hindus read the Ramayana in their own language, recite it at home or in temples, and watch it performed as Ramlila each autumn; Rama's birthday is celebrated as Rama Navami in spring.

fork.setup: you're Vishnu. a demon king can't be killed by any god, and the world is tipping out of balance. what do you do?
options: throw a thunderbolt from the sky.
be born as a human child, in a king's house.
wait for the demon king to grow old.
fork.reveal: he chooses to come down: born as Rama, Dasharatha's son. Hindus call this avatara.

original.note: Sanskrit: the sacrifice (ishti) for the desire (kama) of a son (putra).

trapdoor: what you thought: a king finally gets an heir.
what it means: God comes down. Vishnu is born as Rama, a baby in a worried family's house, to set the world right.
what a scholar hears: avatara, from ava (down) and tri (to cross over); Valmiki's Bala Kanda frames Rama's birth around Ravana's boon, which left out humans.
recall: named for the jaw the thunderbolt struck

Ayodhya.meaning: Dasharatha's shining city on a river

Dasharatha.meaning: the king of Ayodhya; his name means ten chariots

Kaikeyi.meaning: one of Dasharatha's three queens, mother of Bharata

payasa.meaning: sweet rice pudding, sent by the gods in a golden bowl

Vishnu.meaning: the preserver, who comes down as Rama

avatara.meaning: coming down: God born on earth to set things right

Ravana.meaning: the demon king no god could kill

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 15–16 (Ravana's boon leaves out humans; Vishnu agrees to be born as Dasharatha's son)
Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 8–18 (Dasharatha's wish; the sacrifice; the payasa; the four births, Rama on the ninth day of Chaitra)
Bhagavad Gita 4.7–8 (God comes whenever dharma declines; background for avatara, not named in the script)
